newsitem.title: SPAIN: FORECAST - Spain's one-year bills yield seen stable.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Spain's one-year bills yield seen stable.

text.p: The yield on Spanish one-year Treasury bills is expected to remain stable at Wednesday's auction, dealers said on Tuesday.
They added it is likely to be around the 5.172 percent set on February 5, given today's current grey market yields trading around 5.15/5.19 percent.
Low interest by investors was considered the main reason behind expected unchanged yields.
"To reach enough bids the Treasury has to repeat the same (marginal) yield," a dealer in a Madrid bank said.

After the Bank of Spain left its key money market rate unchanged on Friday, despite a fall in January CPI to 2.9 percent from 3.2 percent, dealers took a more cautious view on any possible money market rates decline.
But dealers added recent tensions reflected in money market rates should soon be over as the peseta seems to have found relative stability.
"Rates expectations were not changed. But people are more cautious over the timing of fortcoming cuts," a dealer added.
